Guidance & outlook: On a standalone basis, revenue from operations for FY 2025-26 stood at ₹45,067.80 lakh as against ₹77,226.73 lakh last year.

Consolidated cash and cash equivalents improved to ₹1,594.21 lakh from ₹506.36 lakh, Ask an Indian consumer twenty years ago what she wanted from a bag of rice and the answer would likely have been simple: “That it be clean, and that it be affordable.” FY 2025-26 has been nothing short of an extraordinary year for the Indian agri-processing industry.

Built around two integrated manufacturing units 24 tonnes/day Steam savings achieved through integrated steam-line optimisation 50% Increase in milling capacity Ahmadpur Unit II underwent an important phase of technological modernisation during FY2025-26.
Growth & demand: The direction of the sunrise therefore becomes a quiet reminder that enduring growth begins with strong foundations before extending towards a broader horizon.
Consolidated revenue from operations stood at roughly `64,620 lakh, and consolidated profit after tax increased to about `3,190 lakh, representing growth of more than 50% over the previous year.

Consumers, Employees, Investors, Value Chain Partners Employees, Consumers, Regulators Investors 22 | Halder Venture Limited Natural Capital Human Capital Social & Relationship Capital The launch of UTTAM and continued investment in leadership and safety training strengthened a culture of recognition and capability- building.
Margins & costs: Resource-efficient operations Improving energy utilisation, strengthening process control and creating greater value from agricultural inputs and manufacturing by-products.

100% Food waste diverted from landfill Waste management and circular economy Halder Venture Limited's integrated operating model allows materials generated at one stage of production to become valuable inputs for another.

Disclosure as to maintenance of cost records as specified by the Central Government under section 148 (1) of the Companies Act, 2013: M/s J Pal & Co, Cost Accountants, were appointed as Cost Auditors for the financial year 2025-26.
Capex & expansion: The commissioning of a state-of- the-art solvent extraction plant marked the Company's entry into rice bran oil, strengthening its product portfolio and long-term growth platform.

Our tin manufacturing, tin filling and pouch filling plants came online with a cumulative capacity of 300 MT per day and, following extensive trial runs, began serving markets across Odisha, West Bengal and the North East.
Capital expenditure of roughly `2,516 lakh was focused on bringing this platform into productive use.
Balance sheet & cash: Standalone trade receivables were brought down sharply to ₹9,432.59 lakh from ₹18,207.76 lakh, reflecting a materially tighter credit cycle.

Yet, on the other hand, government export restrictions narrowed market access for Indian rice, while an increase in import duty simultaneously compressed the economics of the edible oil business, Annual Report 2025-26 | 17 Financial StatementsStatutory ReportsCorporate Overview and consolidated operating activities generated a positive cash flow of ₹1,537.17…
Standalone trade receivables were reduced sharply- from over `18,200 lakh to around `9,433 lakh - almost halving the exposure and releasing liquidity back into the system.
Risks & challenges: Despite these challenges, our financial position tells a story of resilience.
Alongside this, we entered into a preliminary understanding to progressively build a partnership with InQube, an agri-technology venture operating in traceability software and carbon sequestration.

Risk management and governance processes were strengthened in anticipation of a larger, more complex organisation, including the ongoing implementation of an enhanced enterprise risk-management framework.
